questions.q: What two estimators does GAE sit between on its bias-variance spectrum?
options: Q-learning and SARSA
The one-step TD error (low variance, biased) and the full Monte Carlo return (unbiased, high variance)
Double DQN and Dueling DQN
PPO and TRPO
questions.explain: GAE generalizes between the one-step TD advantage estimate, which is low variance but biased by critic error, and the full Monte Carlo advantage, which is unbiased but high variance.

questions.q: What does lambda = 0 reduce the GAE formula to?
options: The full Monte Carlo return
Zero for every timestep
The pure one-step TD error, delta_t
The REINFORCE update rule
questions.explain: With lambda = 0, every term in the exponentially-weighted sum beyond delta_t vanishes, leaving just the one-step TD error — the lowest-variance, most-biased end of the spectrum.

questions.q: What does lambda = 1 reduce the GAE formula to?
options: The pure one-step TD error
Zero advantage at every state
The full Monte Carlo advantage estimate, equivalent to G_t - V(s_t)
The DQN loss function
questions.explain: With lambda = 1, the exponentially-weighted sum of TD errors becomes equivalent to the unbiased, high-variance Monte Carlo advantage estimate.

questions.q: Why is GAE computed with a backward pass through the rollout rather than a naive forward summation for each timestep?
options: Because forward summation gives a different, incorrect answer
Because the backward recursion A_t = delta_t + gamma*lambda*A_(t+1) computes the whole sum in linear time instead of quadratic time
Because backward passes are required by PyTorch autograd
Because episodes must always be processed in reverse chronological order for the environment to work
questions.explain: Just like the Monte Carlo return calculation, GAE has a recursive structure that lets it be computed in a single O(T) backward pass rather than O(T^2) forward summation.

questions.q: In the compute_gae function, what is the purpose of the 'mask' variable (1.0 - dones[t])?
options: It doubles the reward at terminal states
It zeroes out the bootstrapped next-value and the recursive GAE term across episode boundaries
It selects which action was taken
It converts rewards into log-probabilities
questions.explain: When a timestep ends an episode, there is no valid next state to bootstrap from, so the mask zeroes out both the next-value term in delta and the recursive gae term so they don't leak across episode boundaries.
